retrievedBy: Carl's overnight session, from arXiv; transcribed from the papers, not from memory
note: Values are copied as printed. Where a paper's own frame is ambiguous it is said here and not resolved.

sources.paper: Venn, Irwin, Shetrone, Tout, Hill, Tolstoy 2004, AJ 128, 1177: Stellar Chemical Signatures and Hierarchical Galaxy Formation
sources.location: Table 3, Velocity Ellipsoids (membership probabilities TN/TK/HL from Gaussian ellipsoids)
sources.criterion: Kinematic probability from Gaussian velocity ellipsoids; columns sigmaU, sigmaV, sigmaW, U, V, W in km/s.
sources.frameNote: V of 220 and 180 for the disks and 0 for the halo is a Galactic-rest-frame V (rotation), not LSR-relative; the paper's Toomre axis is T = sqrt(U^2 + W^2) with extreme-component flags: the text says retrograde V < -200 km/s (Section 2) and, in a later passage, V <= -420 km/s (the two thresholds are printed differently and are not reconciled here), and Toomre T > 340 km/s in both passages. The table is the criterion here, not the flags.

solarMotion.frame: Galactic reference frame (rest frame): the Sun as the paper places it, so V of a disk star is near 220
solarMotion.location: footnote 3 to Section 2: velocities corrected to the Galactic reference frame throughout, (U,V,W)_sun = (9, 232, 7)

sources.paper: Bensby, Feltzing & Oey 2014, A&A 562, A71: Exploring the Milky Way stellar disk

criterion.halo: TD/H < 1 (thick-disk to halo probability ratio) for halo kinematics
criterion.between: 0.5 <= TD/D <= 2: kinematics in between the two disks
criterion.total space velocity guide: vtot = sqrt(U_LSR^2 + V_LSR^2 + W_LSR^2): vtot < 50 km/s mainly thin disk; 70 < vtot < 180 km/s likely thick disk; vtot > 200 km/s likely halo (Toomre-diagram guide, citing Nissen 2004)

sources.frameNote: Asymmetric drifts are relative to the LSR, so V is LSR-relative here (halo -220), unlike Venn Table 3. The paper's sample counts under these criteria: 387 thin, 203 thick, 36 halo, 89 in between (714 stars).

solarMotion.frame: relative to the local standard of rest (the Sun relative to the LSR, added to the heliocentric velocities)
solarMotion.location: Section 3: (U_sun, V_sun, W_sun) = (11.10, 12.24, 7.25) km/s from Schonrich et al. (2010)

sources.countsNote: text of Section 2: 387 thin, 203 thick, 36 halo, 89 in between (sum 715); caption of Fig. 2: 239 potential thick disk stars with TD/D > 2 (203 + 36), 88 in between; the sample is 714 stars

verification.by: a delegated session, against the extracted text of the two PDFs named in sources (sha256 given there)
verification.result: every number of Venn et al. 2004 Table 3 (18 values, 3 rows) and of Bensby et al. 2014 Table A.1 (thin, thick, halo: sigmaU, sigmaV, sigmaW, Uasym, Vasym, X) and every criterion value of Bensby Section 2 (TD/D > 2, TD/D < 0.5, TD/H < 1, vtot < 50, 70 to 180, > 200 km/s, the 387, 203, 36 and 89 counts) matches the paper text; no value was changed
added: sources[0].solarMotion and sources[1].solarMotion: each paper states the solar motion it used to put velocities in its frame (Venn footnote 3 to Section 2; Bensby Section 3). The file as supplied did not carry them; they are copied from the paper text, with the frame each fixes. Needed to apply each criterion in its own frame.

sources[1].countsNote: the paper prints 89 stars in between in the text of Section 2 and 88 in the caption of its Fig. 2; the four text counts sum to 715 for a sample the paper calls 714 stars. The paper is internally inconsistent by one star; neither number is used by any threshold.

sources[0].frameNote is unchanged and still correct: the Table 2 note says UVW are Galactocentric velocities, and the -200 and -420 km/s flags (Section 2, then the conclusions and Section 6 where the second is a V_LSR) are not used by the committed legs.
